submissions.title: Gov. Kotek pauses data centers on state land. Capitol demonstrators want her to go further.
submissions.excerpt: halts easements, rights-of-way, leases, rentals, land-use permits and sales or transfers of state property through July 1, 2027
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Oregon Gov. Tina Kotek issued an executive order (announced Sept 8, 2026) directing state agencies to immediately pause new/unapproved land transactions -- easements, rights-of-way, leases, rentals, land-use permits, sales/transfers -- for data center projects on state-owned property, in effect through July 1, 2027 unless the Governor's Office or Legislature acts sooner. Follows Kotek's August block of a 32-acre state land sale in Salem for a proposed Verrus data center. An Oregon Data Center Advisory Committee is due to deliver policy recommendations by end of 2026. Statewide restriction, not tied to one tracked project -- affects any future project seeking Oregon state land. Checked against agent/daily branches back to 2026-08-25; not previously submitted. submissions.title: NVIDIA Expands AI Infrastructure Capacity in Partnership With Australia's Data Center Ecosystem
submissions.excerpt: supporting the nation's growing demand for AI compute -- with up to a 2-gigawatt buildout by 2027
submissions.suggestedProjectName: NVIDIA Australia AI Infrastructure Partnership (Firmus, Sharon AI, IREN, Megaport, ResetData, CDC, NEXTDC, AirTrunk)
submissions.note: New capacity commitment, not a single-site announcement: NVIDIA announced a partnership with eight Australian data center/cloud operators (Firmus, Sharon AI, IREN, Megaport, ResetData, CDC, NEXTDC, AirTrunk) to expand land, power and shell capacity for NVIDIA DSX AI factories, targeting up to 2 GW buildout by 2027 -- roughly doubling Australia's current ~1.6 GW compute base per coverage. One partner, AirTrunk, already has a tracked project (AirTrunk SYD3, UNDER_CONSTRUCTION) and IREN has tracked US projects (Childress, Sweetwater); this Australia-wide commitment is separate from those specific campuses. Reviewer may prefer a standalone entry for this ecosystem announcement rather than attaching the aggregate 2GW figure to any single tracked project. submissions.title: Trenton Must Place Data-Center-Ban Amendment on Special Election Ballot
submissions.publisher: Court News Ohio (Supreme Court of Ohio)
submissions.excerpt: prohibit construction of new data centers requiring more than 25 megawatts of electricity inside Trenton's boundaries
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: The Ohio Supreme Court ruled Sept 1, 2026 that Trenton (Butler County, OH) must let residents vote on a citizen-initiated charter amendment banning data centers requiring more than 25 MW, after city council had rejected the petition by demanding a higher signature threshold than state law requires. Trenton City Council complied via emergency ordinance Sept 3, 2026, setting a Nov 3, 2026 special election. If approved by voters, no new data center over 25 MW could be built within city limits. Not currently tied to a tracked project, but directly relevant to any developer with interests in Trenton/Butler County, Ohio. Checked against agent/daily branches back to 2026-08-25; not previously submitted.
